fieldValues.title: Actions-token PRs get no CI; dispatch the required checks + dedupe by open PR
fieldValues.summary: schema-sync.yml opens PRs (and now updates branches) with GITHUB_TOKEN, which never fires pull_request/push workflows, so the required checks (Test, Lint, WASM Build, Schema Drift) never ran — the first real poll PR (#978) sat with zero checks and had to be reopened by hand. Added workflow_dispatch to ci.yml and dispatch it directly against the pushed branch right after the push. Also replaced the tag-keyed duplicate guard (which let a later poll open a second PR while an earlier one was still under review, #981) with an open-PR-by-branch-prefix guard that updates the existing branch in place.
fieldValues.body: Dispatched from the srs-rust gate:pool queue via srs#580 tick 2026-09-06 20:1xZ. Fix in srs-rust PR #982: workflow_dispatch added to ci.yml (no other change) and schema-sync.yml's PR step now dispatches it against the branch it just pushed. Real GitHub Actions can't be exercised from the cloud sandbox (workflow_dispatch is only dispatchable once declared on the default branch), so the changed bash was extracted verbatim and dry-run against a local mock git remote with a stubbed gh (real jq evaluating the same --jq filter) across three cases: no open sync PR, an open PR whose content is already current (no-op), and an open PR whose content is stale (update branch in place, dispatch, skip pr create). All three produced the expected git/gh call sequence. The GitHub-side half of the proof is necessarily deferred to the next scheduled poll after merge.
